note: Hand-authored: the shared accept/refuse table for the wpmgr/page-create input with outline_version 3, read by the agent, the control plane and the dashboard. "input" is the exact JSON text. A case with "generate" appends generate.append to that text until it is generate.to_bytes bytes long; JSON allows the trailing whitespace, so only the input size limit (65536 bytes) decides those cases. "agent" is what the agent answers: "ok" or the refusal code. "go" is what the control plane validation must answer before precheck: "accept" or "refuse"; a refusing control plane answers the agent's code, except that an unknown node is the agent's create_content_invalid and the control plane's bad_input. A rule that needs the site carries "site", the facts it needs, and is the agent's alone (go "accept"). A text-character rule (create_content_invalid with go "accept") is the agent's alone too. "rule" names the contract rule the case exercises. A refused case breaks that one rule only, so its code does not depend on the order of the checks. Wire form. Top level: post_type, editor "builder:elementor", elementor_format "classic" (stated), title, outline_version 3, design, page_frame (optional: theme, full_width or canvas), outline. The outline holds sections only: {type "section", anchor, width?, tone?, background? {attachment_id, overlay?, focal?}, spacing?, align?, min_height?, children 1..50}. A section's children are the version 2 leaves (a heading may be level 1, a button style may be text), columns, group and pattern nodes. A pattern is {type "pattern", pattern, variant, ...}. hero and cta hold children (heading, paragraph, buttons, image). The others hold one array of items: features 3-8, testimonials 1-6, plans (pricing) 1-4, faq 1-12, logos 3-10, stats 2-4. The hero is the first child of the first section, and the one h1 of the page lives inside it. The images of a page, backgrounds included, stay within 20.
